body.p: Applicant replies to the Final Rejection dated September 25, 2024, within two months. Claims 1, 6-8, 10, 14, 17, 18, and 20 are presently pending, with claims 1 and 14 being independent. Claims 1, 6, 14, and 20 have been amended. Claims 2-5, 9, 11-13, 15, 16, and 19 have been canceled. Support for the amendments may be found in the originally-filed specification, claims, and figures. No new matter is entered with these amendments. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application.

p.u: uest for Consideration in the AFCP 2.0 Program

body.p: Applicant requests this application to be considered in the AFCP 2.0 program. Applicant believes this response to be compliant with the requirements of 78 Fed. Reg. 29117. Specifically, Applicant submits form PTO/SB/434 with this reply, Applicant asserts that at least one independent claim is amended that does not broaden the scope, and Applicant is willing and available to participate in any interview initiated by the examiner concerning the amendments and remarks herein.

The Office rejects claim 19 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA the Applicant, regards as the invention. Applicant respectfully disagrees with these rejections, but Applicant cancels claim 19 solely in the interest of expediting prosecution.

The Office rejects claims 1 and 6-8 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ta, US Publication No. 2019/0192039 ("Ta") in view of Ben-Haim, US Publication No. 2020/0286225 ("Ben-Haim"), and further in view of Lui, Non-Patent Literature ("Lui (NPL)").
Applicant amends independent claim 1 to further limit the "diffeomorphic smoothing algorithm" to include "computing a parametric coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas,

performing Laplacian smoothing on the parametric coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas to form a smoothed retinotopic coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas, chopping the smoothed retinotopic coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas, and computing, by a Linear Beltrami Solver (LBS), a sensory map for each of the plurality of cortical areas." Support can be found at least in [0051] - [0074].

In the Final Rejection, the Examiner relied on [0023] and [0157] for teaching the specifics of the "diffeomorphic smoothing algorithm" and relied on [0002] for the motivation to modify the teachings of Ta. However, nowhere in Ben Haim is it disclosed or contemplated that a diffeomorphic smoothing algorithm includes "computing a parametric coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas, performing Laplacian smoothing on the parametric coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas to form a smoothed retinotopic coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas, chopping the smoothed retinotopic coordinate for each of the plurality of cortical areas, and computing, by a Linear Beltrami Solver (LBS), a sensory map for each of the plurality of cortical areas" as claimed. Furthermore, as outlined in [0074] of the Present Disclosure, "[i]t was found that with a large amount of added noise, only exemplary methods [the claimed smoothing algorithm] in the present disclosure can achieve diffeomorphic results." Additionally, Applicant asserts that the cited references fail to cure the deficiencies of Ta and Ben Haim. Therefore, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and claim 1, as well as its dependents are in condition for allowance.

The Office rejects claim 10 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ta, Ben- Haim, and Lui (NPL), further in view of U.S Publication No. 2019/0205766 ("Krebs"). Claim 10 depends from independent claim 1. Applicant asserts that Krebs fails to cure the deficiencies of Ta, Ben Haim, and Lui. Accordingly, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn.

The Office rejects claims 14, 17, and 19 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ta in view of Liu, US Publication No. 2016/0292847 ("Liu (US Pub)"), further in view of Liu (NPL). Applicant respectfully disagrees; however, Applicant amends independent claim 14 solely to expedite prosecution.

Applicant amends independent claim 14 to further limit the "processing a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data" to include "processing a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data to produce topological results, wherein the processing comprises: parameterizing the flattened cortical surface to a unit disk to form a parameterized cortical surface; computing, by a segmentation step, a topology preserving segmentation based on the parameterized cortical surface; decoding, by a decoding step, the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data based the topology preserving segmentation and the parameterized cortical surface to form a topological retinotopic map; repeating the segmentation step based on the topological retinotopic map and the decoding step until a theoretically guaranteed convergence occurs; and responsive to the processing, generating a diffeomorphic sensory map, the diffeomorphic sensory map corresponding to the topological retinotopic map after the theoretically guaranteed convergence occurs." Support can be found at least in [0078] - [0107].

Applicant assets that the cited references fail to disclose or contemplate the specifics of the added limitation. More specifically, the cited references fail to disclose or contemplate at least "parameterizing the flattened cortical surface to a unit disk... computing, by a segmentation step, a topology preserving segmentation... decoding, by a decoding step, the functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data based the topology preserving segmentation and the parameterized cortical surface to form a topological retinotopic map; repeating the segmentation step based on the topological retinotopic map and the decoding step until a theoretically guaranteed convergence occurs; and responsive to the processing, generating a diffeomorphic sensory map, the diffeomorphic sensory map corresponding to the topological retinotopic map after the theoretically guaranteed convergence occurs" as claimed. Further, the results [of the claimed method] show that the tRF [the claimed method] not only reduced topology violation (i.e., compatible with neurophysiology conclusions) but also improved/kept the fitting power. Therefore, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn and claim 14 is in condition for allowance
The Office rejects claim 18 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ta, Liu (US Pub), and Liu (NPL), further in view of Krebs. Claim 18 depends from independent claim 14.
Applicant asserts that Krebs fails to cure the deficiencies of Ta, Liu (US Pub), and Liu (NPL). Accordingly, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn.

The Office rejects claim 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Ta, Liu (US Pub), and Liu (NPL), further in view of Wang, US Publication No. 2012/0265050 ("Wang"). Claim 20 depends from independent claim 14. Applicant asserts that Wang fails to cure the deficiencies of Ta, Liu (US Pub) and Liu (NPL). Accordingly, Applicant asserts that the rejection should be withdrawn.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of all rejections. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the Examiner's convenience, if that would help further prosecution of the subject application. This statement does not authorize to charge the issue fee.
